slides.heading: Looping Over Strings
slides.body: Looping Over Strings is part of Definite Iteration. This short lesson gives you a practical Python idea you can understand, try, and reuse in simple programs.

slides.heading: Core Idea: Looping Over Strings
slides.body: A for loop can process each character in a string. This helps you work with text one letter at a time.

slides.heading: Real-World Analogy
slides.body: Looping over a string is like reading a word letter by letter.

annotations.note: This line starts a loop that processes each value in a sequence.
This line displays a value or message on the screen.

slides.heading: Key Rule
slides.body: Use for loops when you want to repeat through a known range or sequence.

slides.heading: Try It Yourself!
slides.prompt: Loop through the string CMU and print each letter.
slides.hint: Use for letter in word: then print(letter).

coding_challenge.prompt_text: Print each character in the word CODE.
coding_challenge.hint_text: Use the idea from the lesson. Keep the code short, readable, and correctly indented.
